title: A 4xx on Drive's pre-upload version check counts as 'may have landed', so S57 keeps the erase in memory instead of putting it back
evidence: Origin: S57's Codex R2. writeDriveRecord's update branch (packages/health-core/src/drive-rest.ts:526-537 on main; drive-rest-record.ts once PR 1676's split lands) wraps driveUpdateIfVersion in one try, and every error but ConflictError becomes uncertain() (:535, LANDED_HINT, :323). driveUpdateIfVersion (drive-rest.ts:278-292; drive-rest-files.ts after the split) first reads the version (driveFileVersion, :245-247, which fails on any non-OK answer) and only then uploads. So a 4xx on that read, before any upload was sent, is reported as a write that may have landed, and S57 keeps the erase in memory instead of putting it back. Fix: move the version check outside the uncertain wrap, perhaps by splitting driveUpdateIfVersion into its check and its upload. Fix with it three comments that still name drive-rest.ts for moved code: packages/health-core/src/write-refusal.ts:49, packages/health-core/src/mcp-hosted-t9-pins.test.ts:6 and :32, ios/engine/entry.ts:259.
